summary: Validated the new Discrepancy Resolve+Undo feature end-to-end on /orders. Backend: all 4 resolve actions (clear/update_date/keep/delete) each produce a discrepancy_undo document and the sibling POST /api/orders/{id}/undo-discrepancy fully reverts order state (items, order_date, status, discrepancy_dismissed) AND the linked dispatch (order_ids / order_fully_dispatched are restored to pre-clear snapshot). Delete-then-undo re-creates the order with the same id. POST /api/orders/{id}/undo-discrepancy with no prior resolution correctly returns 404 'Nothing to undo for this order'. Frontend (UI): orders-filter -> orders-tab-discrepancy renders order-discrepancy-{id} card for the seeded QA order; clicking disc-clear-{id} shows a sonner toast containing an inline 'Undo' action button (clicking it immediately restores the discrepancy card). After leaving the toast, switching to All Status filter reveals the persistent disc-undo-bar-{id} amber chip with disc-undo-btn-{id} ('Timing discrepancy resolved: Cleared · 10/14/2026 Undo'); clicking it removes the bar and restores the discrepancy card. Hindi toggle (lang-btn-hi) correctly translates sidebar + discrepancy card buttons (संभावित तिथि विसंगति / पहले ही डिस्पैच — क्लियर करें / ऑर्डर तिथि अपडेट करें / लंबित रखें / एंट्री हटाएँ) and the undo bar/button key discResolvedAs/discUndo resolve to Hindi text. All QA data (11 customers, 7 dispatches, 1 order) and the temporary qa_tester user were cleaned up at the end.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py resolve_discrepancy() upserts discrepancy_undo but captures only disp_before for the 'clear' action — update_date / keep / delete reversibility relies solely on 'order_before'. That's fine today, but if a future action starts touching dispatches (e.g. update_date aligning dispatch allocations), the undo will silently miss that side-effect. Consider centralising the snapshot (order_before + relevant_dispatch_before + any inventory_delta) in one helper so future actions can't skip it.

undo_discrepancy() uses db.orders.replace_one({id}, before, upsert=True) which is correct for delete-then-undo, but if the order's _id ObjectId was retained in the stored snapshot it would be re-inserted — safer to project {_id:0} when snapshotting (resolve_discrepancy already does this via find_one projection, so it's actually fine; worth a comment noting the invariant).

list_orders() attaches o['discrepancy_undo'] from the undo_map but there's no TTL on discrepancy_undo collection. If users never click Undo, these snapshot documents (full order payload) accumulate forever. Consider a background sweep that deletes entries older than, say, 7 days OR when the order is subsequently edited by any other PATCH path.

Orders.jsx resolveDiscrepancy() shows the toast's Undo action only for the lifespan of the toast (8s). The disc-undo-bar is the only persistent undo surface — that's correct, but worth adding a tooltip/aria-label so screen-reader users understand what 'Undo' refers to without the preceding sentence.
